routeDescriptionClues.description: From Reisavannhytta the route follows cart tracks south to Njahkajohka, partly along the powerline, turns toward the southwest end of Njahkegielas and another vehicle track, crosses a reindeer fence, passes very wet mire, climbs through sparse birch forest and above treeline, briefly comes into Reisa National Park near Rivkkos, passes the Rivkkos summit cairn/viewpoint, crosses/stone-hops Lullehuidjohka, Suvdusjohka, Dæljadasjohka and Suorrebasinjohka, fords Davit Cunujohka, passes near Cunucærro, crosses the Majanasjávri outlet/road area and descends by path through birch forest to Cunovuohppi Fjellstue.

campingAndFire.summary: Treat this as a remote high-plateau stage with limited verified facilities between endpoints. Camping/fire rules depend on whether the traveler is inside Reisa National Park, on Finnmark Estate/outfield, near private cabins or near the legacy Čunovuohppi settlement.
campingNotes: No official tent sites with exact coordinates were verified on section 11.
Allemannsretten / outfield camping principles apply outside protected/private/settlement constraints, including distance from inhabited houses/cabins and leave-no-trace duties.
Do not assume Madam Bongos provides lodging, camping, water or toilet service; UT says the fjellstue is closed.
shelterNotes: Reisavannhytta is the only high-confidence endpoint hut for section 11, but it is a locked reservable Statskog hut.
Ráisjávri Nilut may offer pre-booked accommodation/catering by agreement, but its route proximity and current access/service details need verification.
No verified open hut/gamme was found along the main section 11 line.
fireNotes: Norway's general open-fire/bonfire ban runs 15 April-15 September in/near forest and outfield unless fire risk is clearly absent.
Inside Reisa National Park, vegetation and dead wood are protected; use only fallen twigs where fires are otherwise lawful.
Reisavannhytta has wood/firewood arrangements as hut amenities; this should not be generalized to public firewood along the route.

rules.fire: General Norwegian open-fire ban applies 15 April-15 September in/near forest and outfield unless fire risk is clearly absent. Reisa NP vegetation/dead wood protection also applies inside park portions.
rules.dogs: National/Nordreisa verified leash period is 1 April-20 August. Reindeer sensitivity is important; Kautokeino local extensions were not confirmed in this pass.
rules.huntingFishing: Reisa NP and FeFo fishing/hunting rules apply by area. FeFo inland fishing permits are relevant on Finnmark Estate. Reisaelva salmon and Arctic char fishing remains closed in 2026; that closure is mainly downstream but should inform Reisa-watercourse messaging.
rules.motorAccessSnowmobile: Do not imply public motor access. Reisa NP motor traffic is generally prohibited with limited exceptions. Kautokeino snowmobile trails are regulated and open only when marked/declared open; normal closure from 5 May unless changed.
rules.wasteCamping: Leave-no-trace duties apply. Reisa/FeFo sources prohibit or constrain littering and pollution; hut users must clean after themselves.

safetyHazards: Multiple stream crossings are described; Davit Čunujohka is specifically described as a ford. Crossings may become unsafe after rain or snowmelt.
UT/Enjoy route text describes very wet bog after a reindeer fence and intermittent track/powerline navigation. Do not overstate waymarking or dry-foot conditions.
The section is long and remote, with no confirmed active services between Reisavannhytta and Čunovuohppi. Offline maps, emergency preparedness and conservative route choice are important.
Mobile coverage was not verified from operator maps for the full route corridor; no coverage should be assumed in user-facing text.

conditionReports.title: Hikeouts Nordkalottleden Reisadalen report
conditionReports.summary: After camping by Reisavannhytta on 2024-09-14, the 2024-09-15 day from Raisjavrihytta was 33 km to Goaskinjávri. The author describes the high north's empty plateau, received warnings from other hikers about the last 10 km to Kautokeino being muddy, mosquito-heavy and brushy, and chose to walk the quiet road instead. They camped near Goaskinjávri before continuing 9 km to Kautokeino on 2024-09-15/16.
conditionReports.relevance: Recent late-season field evidence for plateau exposure, road/route choice and warnings about the Kautokeino/Čunovuohppi approach.

conditionReports.summary: Reported Kautokeino to Dealljadasjo as about 26 km in gray, cold, windy weather around 7-8°C, with rain arriving. The first 10 km were on road and two fishers offered transport. The author stopped early because Reisavannhytta was still about 14 km away and found an open hut/cabin on the plateau.
conditionReports.relevance: Recent 2025 condition report for the Kautokeino/Čunovuohppi-to-Ráisjávri corridor: cold summer weather, road walking, long distances and informal/uncertain shelter.

conditionReports.title: Norge på langs 2025, Day 14
conditionReports.summary: Reported Dealljadasjo to Reisavannhytta as 19 km. The day started gray, cold and windy, later clearing and becoming more sheltered. The author chose a slightly different line than planned before rejoining the trail and noted reaching Troms county and Reisavannhytta.
conditionReports.relevance: Recent split-stage evidence for the route corridor east/west of the official section and weather/route-choice caveats.

sourceContradictions.details: Reisa official page lists Reisavannhytta-Madam Bongos as 29 km; Reisa map poster lists Ráisjávri-Čuonovuohppi as 27 km; UT route 136866 gives 27.779 km; OSM/E1 measure about 28.1 km; RouteYou reports 28.2 km; Enjoy mirror reports 43.1 km; UT/NPL child report says 34 km but explicitly includes misnavigation/road route.
sourceContradictions.impact: Use official 29 km as source-reported section distance, but keep section not automated-import-ready until geometry/distance policy is normalized.

sourceContradictions.details: Official Reisa section order is Reisavannhytta to Madam Bongos. OSM relation 9517566, E1 GPX 02.02 and RouteYou are in the opposite Čunovuohppi/Madam Bongos to Ráisjávrihytta direction.
sourceContradictions.impact: Any chosen geometry must be reversed before section import.

sourceContradictions.details: Reisa still uses Madam Bongos fjellstue as an endpoint label. UT route data updated 2025-11-04 says Madam Bongos Fjellstue is closed. Brønnøysund reports the business entity deleted 2019-05-28. Guovdageaidnu strategy calls Čunovuohppi the settlement formerly Madam Bongos fjellstue. OSM still has stale active-hut/service-style tags from older DNT data.
sourceContradictions.impact: Do not import Madam Bongos as active lodging/food/water/toilet. Model as endpoint/access metadata unless current operator evidence is found.

sourceContradictions.details: Reisa cabin page says Ráisjávri Nilut is 200 m from where Nordkalott Trail passes, but the Kartverket coordinate measured about 4 km from OSM relation 9517566.
sourceContradictions.impact: Keep Ráisjávri Nilut pending; geometry or service location must be reconciled before facility import.

sourceContradictions.details: UT route description mentions vehicle tracks, powerline and multiple stone/ford crossings, while fetched OSM relation way tags are only highway=path/foot=designated and do not expose bridge/ford/track features.
sourceContradictions.impact: Route is planning-grade only; named crossings should remain safety metadata until coordinates/currentness are verified.

sourceContradictions.details: UT route text says the route briefly enters Reisa NP near Rivkkos, but exact Reisa NP/Ráisduottarháldi overlap was not GIS-verified.
sourceContradictions.impact: Protected-area rules can be described cautiously; boundary tagging should wait for GIS check.
